executive_summary.headline: Claude Duet launches and the personal-agent race now has four cloud entrants
executive_summary.body: Anthropic opened a Duet research preview on Oct 21 (55,000 likes, 10.6 million views). Grok Bot now phones businesses for you, and Business Insider reports Meta Muse passed 10 million users with shopping as its top use. Peter Yang's side-by-side ranking is the best one-post field guide.

executive_summary.headline: Builders shipped games and mods in a weekend, and published the prompts
executive_summary.body: Pieter Levels had Claude Code write a GTA: San Andreas mission about raising money in SF, then shared the prompt (22,000 likes). Simon Willison shipped Battle Drones, an RTS where two phones sync over sound. Google and DeepMind posted six Gemini 4 Argon builds, from Wizard Chess to a Gothic cathedral.

executive_summary.headline: Open and local models took a big step: Kimi K3.1 Pro, DeepInfer, Flint
executive_summary.body: Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T total, 104B active) is live with open weights due by Nov 4. DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer (43,000 likes). Flint runs a ~40B coding model above 125 tokens per second on a MacBook Pro, and Perplexity Computer now runs fully on a Mac.

executive_summary.headline: AI-for-science posts had a strong week in biology
executive_summary.body: Claude designed 211 protein binders against scorpion toxins and 17 bound in the lab, with all data released. GPT-Rosalind agents scanned millions of mouse-brain cells in 32 minutes and surfaced a DCTN1 cholesterol lead. Warp Sciences raised $215M, and a 124-paper study found Opus 4.8 beat human peer reviewers.

executive_summary.headline: Solo-operator wins keep stacking up
executive_summary.body: Alex Finn reports $1,800 and about 100,000 visitors from a business his Grok Bot built in a week. Greg Isenberg's one-person Muse playbook pulled 1.4 million views, and Tibo says his products since 2024 out-earned his $10M exit. These are the authors' own figures.

top_picks.title: Claude Code wrote a new GTA: San Andreas mission where CJ vibe codes a startup and pitches SF investors
top_picks.author: Pieter Levels
top_picks.summary: Pieter Levels asked Claude Code to build a custom GTA: San Andreas mission about vibe coding a startup and raising money in San Francisco. A follow-up post shares the full prompt so anyone can build their own story mission for the classic PC version on macOS.

secondary_urls.label: Prompt to build your own mission

top_picks.why_it_matters: It shows a coding agent modding a 20-year-old game from a one-line story idea, with the prompt published for others to reuse.
key_takeaways: One-sentence story prompt produced a playable custom mission, per the author.
The follow-up post publishes a reusable prompt for the macOS classic PC version.
Story, dialogue and scripted objectives are all editable by changing the premise.
suggested_actions: Paste the published prompt into your coding agent and swap in a mission about your own business.
Run the same approach on any mod-friendly game you already own.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: mod a game you love as a custom story for a friend, a client or a launch teaser. Try it: use the published prompt, change the premise to your product, and send the result as your next holiday card.

top_picks.title: Simon Willison ships Battle Drones, a browser RTS that syncs two phones over sound
top_picks.author: Simon Willison
top_picks.summary: Willison built a Command & Conquer style RTS that runs in the browser and works offline as a PWA. Two nearby devices sync game state through audio messages with no game server. His write-up counts 321 commits across 12 iterations, mostly Claude Code with Opus 5.5, and says he reviewed almost none of the code.

secondary_urls.label: French fork with new models and music

top_picks.why_it_matters: A solo developer with little game experience shipped a complete multiplayer game in about three months, and a fork with new art appeared within a day.
key_takeaways: Prototype began in July; the Oct 20 post covers 12 major iterations and 321 commits.
Audio-link multiplayer came from Claude building a bandwidth probe, then an audio modem; online play uses a stateless WebSocket relay.
A mode lets two LLMs play each other; Ultracode mode ran more than 1,000 simulated playtests to rebalance units.
A French fork adds new 3D models, music and a cinematic intro.
suggested_actions: Play Battle Drones on a phone, then try the two-device audio mode.
Ask your coding agent for a small multiplayer toy with no server, using sound or QR codes to sync.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ship a playable thing in public and let strangers fork it. Try it: build a tiny game for your community in a weekend, publish the prompts, and invite remixes.

top_picks.title: Perplexity Computer now runs fully local on a Mac, with the model and agent on-device
top_picks.author: Perplexity
top_picks.summary: Perplexity Computer can run entirely on a Mac, working with native apps and local files without sending data to the cloud. It is available now in the Perplexity Mac app.
top_picks.why_it_matters: The model and the agent both run on your Mac, so it works on native apps and local files without sending that data to the cloud.
key_takeaways: Available now in the Perplexity Mac app.
Works with native Mac apps and local files.
Both the model and the agent run on-device, per Perplexity.
suggested_actions: Update the Perplexity Mac app and try it on a folder of local files.
Run one weekly chore, such as sorting downloads or summarizing notes, fully offline.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give an agent your messy local folder and let it work without leaving your machine. Try it: point Perplexity Computer at your Downloads folder and ask it to sort, rename and summarize.

top_picks.title: Gemini 4 Argon builds a playable 3D Wizard Chess game with a multi-agent Blender workflow
top_picks.author: Gemini App
top_picks.summary: The Gemini app account shows a playable 3D Wizard Chess game built from scratch with Gemini 4 Argon in Google Antigravity in the Gemini app for Mac. The agents coordinate a Blender workflow to model, design and animate in real time. Google and DeepMind posted five more Argon builds the same week: a desk photo turned into a playable 3D track, a periodic table synced to a song, an anatomy viewer, real-time fur, and a Gothic cathedral scene.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A single prompt can now produce a modelled, animated, playable 3D scene, and Google keeps publishing prompts people can copy.
key_takeaways: Built with Antigravity inside the Gemini app for Mac, per the post.
Agents split modelling, design and animation across a Blender workflow.
Companion demos start from a single photo or one Nano Banana image.
suggested_actions: Photograph your desk or a product shelf and ask Argon to turn it into a playable scene.
Rebuild a board game you own as a 3D version for your kids or your customers.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: turn a physical thing into an interactive toy. Try it: photograph your product or your desk, ask Argon to make it a playable 3D game, and send the link to three friends.
top_picks.recurrence_note: Gemini 4 Argon launched earlier in October; this week brought consumer-facing build demos.

top_picks.title: Peter Yang ranks the four personal agents: Grok Bot, Muse, Claude Duet and ChatGPT Dots
top_picks.author: Peter Yang
top_picks.summary: Yang lists pros and cons for each agent. Grok Bot has the easiest mental model and free X access; Muse has the best consumer UX and business calling; Claude Duet is the most proactive out of the box; ChatGPT Dots works inside ChatGPT but is still buggy. He keeps no more than four connected to his email.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run the same three real errands through two agents and keep the one that finishes them. Try it: book a dinner, summarize an inbox and reorder a household item with each.

sections.title: Tool Announcements
sections.description: New products, models and features announced on X this week, ordered by priority.

items.title: Grok Bot can now phone a person or business, make a request and send you a summary
items.author: Elon Musk
items.summary: Musk announced that Grok Bot can call someone or a business for you, make a request on your behalf, take notes on the response and message you a summary. He posted it Oct 25.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hand the phone call you dread to an agent. Try it: ask it to call a local shop for hours, price and stock, and read the note it sends back.

items.title: Claude sessions on web, desktop and mobile switch to auto mode by default next week
items.author: Claude
items.summary: Starting next week, Claude sessions on Pro, Max and Team plans run in auto mode by default, so work keeps moving without an approval click at each step. Manual mode stays one switch away.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference stack serving V4.1-Flash
items.author: DeepSeek
items.summary: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, its in-house inference framework that powers DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at scale, and published the repo on GitHub. The company says it aims to lower compute costs and energy use.

items.title: Mercury 3 diffusion LLM beats GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on quality at 1,000+ tokens per second
items.author: Stefano Ermon
items.summary: Inception released Mercury 3, a diffusion language model with a 1M-token context that the company says outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 while running above 1,000 tokens per second. It is available on the Inception API, Baseten and OpenRouter.

items.title: Cursor agents can now drive desktop apps such as the iOS Simulator to test what they build
items.author: Cursor
items.summary: Cursor added computer control so agents can operate desktop apps, including the iOS Simulator, and test the features they just built.

items.title: Canva Craft puts a design-specific image model in everyone's hands
items.author: Canva
items.summary: Canva introduced Craft, its first frontier model built for design, and says it ranks second among AI labs for image generation on the DesignArena leaderboard. Image generation is available to everyone.

items.title: Mistral launches Voxtral 3 transcription and speech models behind a new voice agents API
items.author: Mistral AI
items.summary: Mistral introduced Voxtral 3, transcribe and speech models that power its new voice agents API.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, a 4GB open model for local assistants and robots
items.author: NVIDIA AI
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, a small open model for local assistants, interactive characters and robots. In the demo, Bolt handles conversation and Cosmos handles vision on a Reachy Mini, both running on a Jetson Orin Nano 8GB.
items.recurrence_note: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt family first covered Oct 12; this adds the 4GB E4B variant.

items.title: Flint, a ~40B MoE coding model, runs at 125+ tokens per second on a MacBook Pro via Ollama
items.author: Ollama
items.summary: Ollama added Flint from Recursive SI, a ~40B-parameter mixture-of-experts open model for on-device agentic coding that generates over 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro. It launches with one command, including as a model for Claude Code.

items.title: Gemini arrives in Google Maps navigation on CarPlay for parking, incidents and rerouting
items.author: Google
items.summary: Gemini is now available in Google Maps navigation on CarPlay: ask it to find parking, report a traffic incident or change your route by voice.

items.title: Hermes Agent gets an official Meshy plugin to generate printable and game-ready 3D models
items.author: Nous Research
items.summary: Hermes Agent now has an official plugin for Meshy: ask for a 70-thousand-polygon treasure chest for Godot or turn a photo of a mug into a printable model. Models render in chat in Hermes Desktop, and on messaging apps it sends a preview video.

items.title: ChatGPT Slides adds real-time co-editing, comments and on-slide editing
items.author: ChatGPT
items.summary: ChatGPT Slides now supports sharing decks, editing together in real time and leaving comments, with on-slide editing of text, charts and images. Decks export to PowerPoint or Google Slides.

items.title: Claude adds MCP Tasks so plugins can run long jobs such as deep research and report back
items.author: ClaudeDevs
items.summary: Claude now supports MCP Tasks and Elicitations. Tasks let Claude hand plugins long-running jobs like deep research and get a report when they finish.

items.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation, next to MCP
items.author: ClaudeDevs
items.summary: Anthropic is donating the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation, where MCP already lives. The post says 70+ agent platforms have integrated it since December 2025, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and VS Code.

items.title: OpenAI API adds 12-hour prompt caching so always-on agents like dots reuse context at the cached rate
items.author: OpenAI Developers
items.summary: The OpenAI API now lets developers choose 12-hour prompt caching, so persistent agents such as dots keep shared instructions, tools and context cached longer and pay the lower cached-input rate between requests hours apart.

items.title: Claude Duet opens as a proactive agent that briefs you each morning and works while you are away
items.author: Claude
items.summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, an app where Claude brings you what needs attention, finishes tasks you assign, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before it acts. The product page says it is built for professionals and small-business owners, runs on Claude Opus 5.5 in its own cloud VM, and connects to more than 6,000 plugins. Waitlist access is open to US Pro and Max subscribers.
items.why_it_matters: A summary by Baoyu (@dotey) counts it as the fourth cloud personal agent since August, after Grok Bot, Muse and ChatGPT Dots, and the one pitched at owner-operators with invoicing, payroll and store tools wired in.
key_takeaways: Sends a short morning brief and checks connected accounts every few hours, per the Anthropic article.
Runs in a cloud VM with its own browser, so it keeps working with your laptop closed.
Pays for business items through Link with a one-time virtual card after you approve the spend.
Included in Pro and Max, sharing existing usage limits; no separate price is listed.
suggested_actions: Write down the three Monday-morning checks you do by hand and draft them as the brief you want Duet to send.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a morning brief that arrives before you ask, covering inbox, invoices and calendar in one message. Try it: this week, hand-write the five-line brief you wish you got every day, then use it as the spec for whichever agent you run.
items.recurrence_note: Personal-agent launches (Grok Bot, Muse, Dots) featured in earlier weeks; Duet is the new entrant.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro arrives as a 2.8T-parameter open-weight model with weights due by Nov 4
items.author: Moonshot AI (Kimi)
items.summary: Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro, a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 2.8T total and 104B active parameters and a 1M-token context. It targets full-project game coding in Unreal, Unity and Godot and parametric 3D modeling in Blender and CAD. Artificial Analysis scores it fourth on its Intelligence Index at 55, and says it will lead open-weight models once the weights ship.
items.why_it_matters: Artificial Analysis expects it to be the top open-weight model once weights ship, and it is aimed at builders of games, 3D assets and CAD parts. A 2-3x faster Highspeed tier is live now.
key_takeaways: Live today on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the API; full weights promised by Nov 4, 2026.
Tech blog reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 66.4% for Claude Opus 5.5.
Claim-level hallucination rate on its hard benchmark falls from 23.4% to 8.3%, per Moonshot.
Pricing and license are not stated on the blog page.
suggested_actions: Ask K3.1 Pro to build a small Godot or Blender project and compare it with your current model.
Bookmark the Nov 4 weights date to try a quantized local run.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: use a model that can model parts, not just write code. Try it: give it a photo and dimensions of an object on your desk and ask for a parametric CAD file you can 3D print.

sections.title: Key Insights
sections.description: Wins, playbooks and borrowable ideas from builders, creators and indie operators.

items.title: Alex Finn reports his Grok Bot built an autonomous business with $1,800 in revenue and about 100,000 visitors
items.author: Alex Finn
items.summary: Finn says a business his Grok Bot built a week earlier has earned $1,800, drawn almost 100,000 visitors and 200,000 page views, and gathered 3,000 newsletter subscribers. He lists a six-step recipe: pick a challenge your audience has, have the agent build and maintain the site and newsletter, wire in Resend, Vercel, Stripe and GitHub, and promote it on social.
items.why_it_matters: It packages a repeatable recipe for a one-person content business that an agent builds and runs, with numbers the author published.
key_takeaways: Figures are the author's own: $1,800, about 100,000 visitors, 200,000+ page views, 3,000 subscribers.
Follow-up post says 60% of views come from X and 40% from SEO and AEO.
Stack named: Resend, Vercel, Stripe, GitHub as agent plugins.
suggested_actions: Ask your agent to list ten recurring questions your audience asks, then pick one to turn into a small site.
Publish the site and a newsletter signup the same day, then post it where your audience already is.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let an agent own a small content product end to end while you handle distribution. Try it: choose one niche question you answer often and have your agent stand up a site, a newsletter and a Stripe link by Friday.
items.recurrence_note: Grok Bot builder stories appeared in the Oct 5 edition; this is a new result thread with traffic and subscriber numbers.

items.title: Meta Muse passes 10 million users in about six weeks, with shopping the top use
items.author: Business Insider
items.summary: Business Insider reports that Meta's Muse app has passed 10 million users since launch, and that Mark Zuckerberg called shopping its top use. An analyst summary of the Q3 call says about 25% of those users are daily active and average purchases run above $200.

secondary_urls.label: Analyst summary of the Meta Q3 call

items.recurrence_note: Meta Muse was a Top Pick on Sep 21; this week adds adoption numbers.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: make your shop easy for someone else's agent to buy from. Try it: this week, check that your product pages, prices and stock are readable in plain text, then ask a personal agent to buy something from you.
key_takeaways: 10 million users set up agents in the first month and a half in the US and Canada, per the earnings-call summary.
Shopping is the top use, with average purchases above $200.
The call summary says Meta is building an open protocol for consumer agents to talk to business agents.
items.why_it_matters: A free consumer agent reached 10 million setups faster than Threads did at launch, per the call summary, and people are using it to buy things.

items.title: Greg Isenberg lays out a one-person Muse business he says can start with $0 and no following
items.author: Greg Isenberg
items.summary: Isenberg argues Muse creates a rare arbitrage for solo operators and posts a step-by-step plan for a one-person business powered by Muse. The thread drew 1.4 million views.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pick the newest free agent platform and build a niche service on it before the crowd arrives. Try it: spend one evening listing three tasks a local business pays for and see which one Muse can deliver.

items.title: Matt Wolfe lets Claude edit an entire video with one prompt and no instructions
items.author: Matt Wolfe
items.summary: Wolfe dragged in his talking-head A-roll plus a link to Kimi's launch video, and Claude reused the editing skill from his previous video to cut the whole thing, adding music from ElevenLabs. It is his second fully AI-edited video; the first was done in Claude Code without DaVinci Resolve.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: save your editing process as a reusable skill and let the agent run it on every new recording. Try it: edit one video with an agent this week and keep the skill file for the next one.

items.title: Peter Yang releases /video-short, a free agent skill that turns a raw recording into a polished short
items.author: Peter Yang
items.summary: Yang published /video-short on GitHub. It works with your preferred AI agent to add B-roll, motion graphics, captions, AI video and music, and includes a review page for giving frame-level feedback.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a review page where you comment on frames turns an agent into an editor you can direct. Try it: install the skill and cut one 30-second short from a recording you already have.

items.title: Justine Moore asks Grok Bot for a video about itself and it storyboards, cuts and scores the whole thing
items.author: Justine Moore
items.summary: Moore says Grok Bot set the storyline, found clips, cut and stitched them, and added titles and music. She singled out the ending for its sense of humor.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask an agent to make a video about your own product and see what story it picks. Try it: give your agent your landing page and ask for a 45-second explainer with music.

items.title: Jensen Huang closes GTC Berlin with Hermes Agent building and training a robot duck course
items.author: Nous Research
items.summary: Huang installed a customized Hermes Agent in one prompt on an NVIDIA RTX Spark, then had it plan an obstacle course, have GPT-6 Astra build it with FreeCAD, Omniverse, Blender, Newton and Isaac Lab, and train thousands of simulated Hugging Face Microducks until a validated policy was ready for the real robot.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask an agent to build the agent you want. Try it: describe your ideal helper in one paragraph and have your current agent install and configure it.

items.title: Guillermo Rauch: ask a coding agent for an explainer, deploy it and share the link
items.author: Guillermo Rauch
items.summary: Rauch says AI can now create the most engaging explainers in the world and points to builder Dilum Sanjaya's work. He suggests vetted visualization platforms, repair-the-system games and quizzes as follow-on ideas.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: turn one thing you explain over and over into an interactive page. Try it: ask a coding agent for an explainer of your most common customer question and deploy it.

items.title: Farza's launch-video approach: make launches routine, not rare, high-budget events
items.author: Y Combinator
items.summary: Y Combinator profiles Farza, founder of Clicky and former Buildspace head, who treats launch videos as part of the everyday process instead of rare, expensive productions. His posts regularly reach millions of views.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: post a small launch every week instead of one big one. Try it: record a 60-second phone video of whatever you shipped this week and post it today.

items.title: Tibo says his products since 2024 have earned more than his 2022 $10M exit
items.author: Tibo
items.summary: Tibo reports that after selling a startup for $10M in 2022 and restarting from zero in 2024, his products have now made more than the exit did. The post is a short self-reported milestone.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ship a portfolio of small products rather than one big bet. Try it: list three small tools your audience already asks for and build the quickest one this week.

items.title: Unsloth shrinks DeepSeek V4.1-Flash to 250GB so it runs locally on a 128GB+ RAM machine
items.author: Unsloth
items.summary: Unsloth released 1-bit quantized DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 that it says keeps about 88.2% accuracy while cutting size from 508GB to 250GB, a 52% reduction. It calls V4.1 Flash 1017 the strongest open model to date and links a guide and GGUF files.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run a frontier-class open model on your own box. Try it: follow the Unsloth guide on a 128GB machine and compare it with your usual API model on five of your real prompts.

items.title: Garry Tan's GBrain adds a personal plan so Claude, Codex and Capy share one memory
items.author: Garry Tan
items.summary: Tan says agents should not each start from zero, and that GBrain's new personal plan for founders lets Claude, Codex and Capy share one memory of who you know and how you execute.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give all your agents one shared memory file. Try it: write a one-page "how I work and who I know" note and paste it into each agent you use.

sections.title: AI for Science
sections.description: Lab, biology, physics and Earth-science results from AI systems, plus the demos that make science fun.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon builds a 3D periodic table synced to Tom Lehrer's "The Elements"
items.author: Google DeepMind
items.summary: DeepMind shows a 3D periodic table created in Antigravity that animates orbiting electrons, atomic data and light spectra in time with Tom Lehrer's song.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: turn reference data into a toy that teaches itself. Try it: take a dataset you know well and ask Argon for an interactive visualization with a soundtrack.

items.title: Warp Sciences raises $215M Series A to bring frontier AI and robotics into the drug lab
items.author: Kevin Weil
items.summary: Kevin Weil announced Warp Sciences, a company applying AI and robotics to develop medicines faster, with a $215M Series A led by Lightspeed. His co-founders are Dev Patil, FAIR co-founder Manohar Paluri and drug hunter Sol Reisberg.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: put the model next to the instrument, not just in a browser. Try it: list one measurement you repeat by hand and sketch how an agent could read its output.

items.title: Study of 124 Harvard social-science papers finds Opus 4.8 beats human experts as peer reviewers
items.author: Ethan Mollick
items.summary: Mollick shares a study across 124 Harvard social-science papers, from statistical analyses to formal models to qualitative work, in which Opus 4.8 beat human experts as peer reviewers on every measure. He argues academics must adapt the practice of science to AI quickly.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run an AI review pass before any human sees your draft. Try it: paste your next report into a strong model with a reviewer prompt and fix what it flags.

items.title: DeepMind's ForTy maps natural, planted and farmed forests at 10 metres, free on Earth Engine
items.author: Google DeepMind
items.summary: Forest Typology (ForTy) is a 10m map of natural, planted and farmed forests built on AlphaEarth Foundations. The 2020 map and the 2017-2025 time series are published in Scientific Data and free on Google Earth Engine.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pull a free, current map layer into your own planning. Try it: open ForTy in Earth Engine and overlay a region you care about.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Flora open weights, a robotics data engine at 125x lower cost
items.author: Jim Fan
items.summary: Jim Fan says his group built a robotics data engine with Astra-level performance at 125x lower cost and open-sourced the weights. Flora already labels 200K hours of video a day on 500 GPUs, with timestamped captions for curating egocentric human footage.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: use cheap video labelers to turn raw footage into training data. Try it: run Flora on an hour of your own workshop or kitchen video and look at the captions.

items.title: Google Research publishes its Personal Health Agent in Nature and open-sources it
items.author: Google Research
items.summary: Google Research marks the Personal Health Agent (PHA) paper in Nature, and open-sourced the work. A quoted post says it is the multi-agent architecture behind Google Health Coach, orchestrating specialized agents across wearable and biomarker data.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: split a personal-data assistant into specialists for sleep, activity and labs. Try it: build a three-agent health journal on your wearable export.

items.title: Mistral and NVIDIA team up on physics AI: faster simulation, open benchmarks and datasets for CAE and EDA
items.author: Mistral AI
items.summary: Mistral announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to bring AI to industrial engineering: faster simulation, open benchmarks and supporting datasets for physics AI, and evaluations for agentic AI in computer-aided engineering and electronic design automation.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let an agent run simulation sweeps you used to queue for days. Try it: pick one parametric study you run by hand and ask an agent to script the sweep and chart the results.

items.title: Claude designed 211 protein binders against scorpion venom toxins; 17 bound in the lab
items.author: Anthropic
items.summary: An internal research Claude model designed minibinders against five scorpion neurotoxins in 64 hours, generating 318,484 designs before selecting 211 to test. Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience found 17 binders, and the two best bind the Mexican scorpion toxin Cn2 in the single-digit nanomolar range. Anthropic released all 211 designs and the lab data.
items.why_it_matters: It is an end-to-end design campaign run by a model, measured in a wet lab, with every design and result published for others to build on.
key_takeaways: Claude worked on its own for 24 hours after the first prompt, then took four follow-ups.
11 of 60 single-toxin designs bound (18%); 17 of 211 overall met the binder criteria.
Binding was measured against recombinant toxins; neutralization testing is the next step.
Dataset and technical report are public.
suggested_actions: Download the 211-design dataset and look at which hotspot choices produced binders.
Run a small design campaign on a protein target in your own field using the same open tools.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let an agent run a full design-test loop and publish the raw data so others can learn from the misses. Try it: pick one measurable design problem you own and write the loop as a prompt plus a scoring function.

items.title: GPT-Rosalind agents read millions of mouse-brain cells in 32 minutes and surface a DCTN1 cholesterol lead
items.author: OpenAI
items.summary: With PerturbAI and Scripps Research, thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents linked gene-expression results from millions of mouse brain cells to the literature in 32 minutes and proposed that disrupting DCTN1 may impair cholesterol transport in neurons. OpenAI calls it a lead to test, and says the collaboration is expanding to new drug-target searches.
items.why_it_matters: Distributed agents cited more than 700 references at the largest workload against 11 for a single agent, and blinded experts preferred their reports 75% of the time, per OpenAI.
key_takeaways: The findings are proposed mechanisms, and OpenAI is expanding the collaboration to test them and search for new drug targets.
Human experts judged the DCTN1-cholesterol hypothesis novel and worth following up.
The reasoning atlas is available for scientists to explore.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: fan out hundreds of reading agents across one big dataset and merge their reports. Try it: split your last quarter of customer feedback into 200 chunks, have an agent read each, then synthesize.
suggested_actions: Read the OpenAI write-up and explore the reasoning atlas.
Try a fan-out of reading agents on one of your own large datasets.

sections.title: Fun Finds
sections.description: Playful demos worth trying this weekend.

items.title: Messi asked ChatGPT for a chess opening that fits his style; it suggested Goat Horns
items.author: ChatGPT
items.summary: ChatGPT's account shares that Lionel Messi asked ChatGPT to teach him a chess opening that matched his playing style, and it suggested one called Goat Horns.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask an assistant to match a skill to your personality. Try it: ask for a chess opening, a workout or a recipe that fits how you play, train or cook.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon turns a single Nano Banana image into a 3D Gothic cathedral via Blender MCP
items.author: Google DeepMind
items.summary: From one Nano Banana image, Argon drives Blender MCP in an autonomous loop inside Antigravity, sculpting Gothic architecture, aligning camera grids and staging audio-reactive lighting. DeepMind and Google posted two versions of the demo.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: go from one picture to a full scene. Try it: generate a single image of a place you want to build and ask Argon to model it in Blender.

items.title: A photo of a real desk becomes a playable 3D racetrack with Gemini 4 Argon
items.author: Google
items.summary: Google photographed a desk and had Argon orchestrate subagents, Blender MCP and Nano Banana to turn everyday objects into a playable 3D track.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: scan your room into a game level. Try it: photograph your desk, hand it to Argon and race a toy car around your own stapler.

items.title: ChatGPT fills a photo of an empty bookshelf with real books chosen for you
items.author: Justine Moore
items.summary: Moore notes you can give ChatGPT a photo of an empty bookshelf and ask it to fill the shelves with real books based on what it knows about you, and calls it a fun showcase for image generation.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: use image generation for a visual of a space you are planning. Try it: photograph an empty wall and ask for it filled with art and objects that fit you.

items.title: RTX Remix comes to Minecraft Java Edition with path-traced lighting for creators
items.author: NVIDIA
items.summary: NVIDIA released RTX Remix for Minecraft: Java Edition, giving creators tools to remaster the game with path-traced lighting and AI-powered DLSS, available on GeForce and RTX Spark.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: remaster a world you love with new lighting. Try it: load your favorite Minecraft world in RTX Remix and film a 20-second flythrough.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon codes a real-time 3D fur engine that runs in your browser
items.author: Google
items.summary: Argon coded a custom WebGL2 fur engine in Antigravity, with an automatic lightweight fallback, GPU groom shaders, procedural character meshes and animation for live hair physics.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask for a physics toy rather than a static page. Try it: request a browser demo of something that moves, like hair, cloth or water, and share the link.

sections.title: Viral Breakouts
sections.description: High-engagement posts from the viral sweep: at least 5,000 likes, 1 million views or 1,000 reposts.

items.title: Codex Day 18 update: Decisions API is GA, OpenResponses joins the Linux Foundation, and usage resets
items.author: Tibo
items.summary: Tibo (@thsottiaux) posts in his numbered Codex update series that the Decisions API is generally available, OpenResponses joined the Linux Foundation, performance improved and Uber is going all in on Codex and work, followed by a usage reset. The post drew 1.9 million views.

items.title: Thariq leaves Anthropic after more than a year building Claude Code and plans a break
items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Thariq says he has left Anthropic after more than a year on Claude Code, praising colleagues, and plans a break before starting something new. The post reached 5.3 million views and 30,600 likes. He points readers to Boris Cherny, Addy Osmani, Lydia Hallie, Cat Wu and ClaudeDevs for Claude Code content.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon processed about 25 trillion tokens in its first 72 hours
items.author: Logan Kilpatrick
items.summary: Logan Kilpatrick says Gemini 4 Argon processed roughly 25 trillion tokens in the 72 hours after launch, and that demand for intelligence is still under-appreciated.

sections.title: Hot Takes
sections.description: Two live debates: which personal agent to live in, and how much to hand an agent at once.

items.title: Position: Grok Bot is the daily always-on agent for almost every task and keeps getting better
items.author: Chubby
items.summary: Chubby calls Grok Bot his daily always-on set of agents for almost every task, says it is "insanely good" and improves almost daily.
items.why_it_matters: Opposite call to Peter Yang's ranking, where Grok Bot's email feature does not work yet.

items.title: Position: Claude Duet is the most proactive and polished, with arguably the best model behind it
items.author: Peter Yang
items.summary: Yang, who had early access, says Duet is the most proactive agent he has used and makes the case in a video that Artifacts may be its secret sauce. In his written ranking he adds that it is polished and simple but lacks research-preview features such as driving its browser, that Grok Bot's email feature does not really work, and that ChatGPT Dots is still buggy.

items.title: Position: hand a big job to an agent and let it rip; it beat a two-year human rewrite
items.author: Peter Steinberger
items.summary: Steinberger says agents now deliver in weeks what Microsoft needed a team and two years to do for the TypeScript compiler, and argues you can just let an agent rip on a whole rewrite.

items.title: Position: slow down and give agents one P0 at full attention
items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Thariq says most agent multitasking produces work that will not matter and that one priority at full attention beats many parallel threads.

emerging_signals.pattern: Personal agents become a category with a device to match
emerging_signals.evidence: Per a Chinese-language summary by Baoyu (@dotey), Grok Bot (Aug 11), Muse (Sep 8), ChatGPT Dots (Sep 29) and Claude Duet (Oct 21) all give you a cloud computer that works while you are away. Alex Finn posted twice about the new iPhone Duo as the way to manage them, and Grok Bot added phone calls this week.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Which agent opens to the most users first: Duet is US-only by waitlist, while Muse has 10 million setups.

emerging_signals.pattern: Gemini 4 Argon is being sold on visual, playable builds
emerging_signals.evidence: Google, Gemini App and DeepMind posted a Wizard Chess game, a desk-to-track game, a fur engine, a periodic table, an anatomy viewer and a cathedral between Oct 19 and Oct 23, all in Antigravity with Blender MCP. Logan Kilpatrick says it processed about 25 trillion tokens in 72 hours.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether independent creators reproduce these builds and post their prompts.

emerging_signals.pattern: Agents run full science loops and publish the data
emerging_signals.evidence: Claude ran a 64-hour protein design campaign with wet-lab testing, GPT-Rosalind agents scanned millions of cells in 32 minutes, and a Harvard study put Opus 4.8 ahead of expert reviewers. Warp Sciences and OpenAI's Orchestra Bio acquisition show labs moving toward drug development.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: First wet-lab confirmation of the DCTN1 cholesterol lead, and neutralization tests for the scorpion binders.

emerging_signals.pattern: Capable models now fit on a laptop
emerging_signals.evidence: Flint (~40B MoE, 125+ tokens per second on an M4 Pro), Muse Glimmer (30B, one consumer GPU), Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B (4GB), Unsloth's 250GB 1-bit DeepSeek V4.1-Flash, and Perplexity Computer fully local on Mac.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Kimi K3.1 Pro weights on Nov 4 and the first community quantizations.

suggested_refinements.notes: Access: X search and the logged-in timeline were not available. Posts were collected through a public timeline mirror (api.fxtwitter.com) for about 130 handles, plus web search limited to x.com; the viral sweep therefore covers posts from handles I queried and from search hits, not all of X. Every Top Pick and section post was refetched for text and counts (likes, replies, reposts, views) between about 00:40 and 01:15 UTC on Oct 26, and the Top Pick links to Anthropic, Simon Willison, Claude, OpenAI and Kimi were opened and read. Window used: Oct 19 04:00 UTC to Oct 26 04:00 UTC; posts from the last evening of Oct 25 Pacific time are not captured. Curated-list gaps: @karpathy, @JeffDean, @OriolVinyalsML, @ylecun and @JackClarkSF returned no posts in the window and @xai returned a server error; @ibab, @aider_ai, @windsurf_ai and @CrewAIInc were not queried. Not enough weeks of data to recommend dropping any handle. Materials-discovery and building-science posts were thin on X this week; the clearest materials item found (MIT news on Oct 18, a crystal-structure model) predates the window and has no qualifying X post, so it is not included. Items outside this desk's remit were left out of this one. Freshness: no post repeats last week's edition; 5 of 65 index rows continue a theme (Duet, Grok Bot builder stories, Argon, Muse, Nemotron) and are tagged returning_theme, so pct_new is 0.92 against the 0.80 target. Engagement is as observed at fetch time and will keep rising. Alex Finn, Tibo and Greg Isenberg figures are the authors' own.
